title: Security configuration bypass through the unauthenticated admin config endpoint
summary: Security controls for every later invoice are removed or weakened until the configuration is reset. Fraudulent invoices are approved more easily. The same endpoint also accepts custom_goals.

LC.rationale: An unauthenticated POST to the admin config endpoint writes attacker-supplied configuration and custom_goals natural language directly into the system prompt that drives tool invocation, with no mediation or validation.

CP.rationale: The manipulated FinBotConfig row persists in the database and is re-injected into the system prompt of every later invoice run, surviving the originating session.

AP.rationale: A single agent relays the compromised configuration into its own tool decisions (approve_invoice) within the same application and principal domain; no trust boundary to another agent or tenant is crossed.

RH.rationale: The agent's approval decisions sit on a proxy/flag path (invoice approved under stated conditions), but no human-verified reward-hacking episode is documented in the packet.

ES.rationale: Only five fixed tools are defined in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills on the path.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice-processing agent whose goals and tool choices are directed by the model, with the rule-based fallback only when no OpenAI client exists, which is not the documented default.
